title: Asshole – rules
sub: The card game where the winner becomes king and the loser has to serve. Learn it in five minutes, play it all night.

seo.rulesT: Asshole card game rules – simply explained
seo.rulesD: How to play Asshole: dealing, beating cards, ranks from king to asshole, the card swap between rounds, popular variants and FAQ.

rules.goal: The goal: get rid of all your cards as fast as you can. Whoever is left holding cards at the end is the asshole – and has to hand their best cards to the king in the next round.
rules.setupLead: You need one ordinary pack of cards, no jokers, and 3 to 8 players. Four to six is the most fun. In Germany the game is usually played with a 32-card Skat pack.
rules.rankLead: The 7 is the lowest card, the ace the highest. Suits (♠♥♦♣) don't matter: a 9 of hearts is worth exactly as much as a 9 of spades.
rules.rankAlt: Order from low to high: 7, 8, 9, 10, jack, queen, king, ace.
rules.rankP: J = jack, Q = queen, K = king, A = ace. With 52 cards the 2 is the lowest, followed by 3, 4, 5, 6 and then as above.
rules.dealP: Shuffle and deal all cards one at a time, clockwise. If they don't divide evenly, some players get one card more – that's fine. Everyone sorts their hand and keeps it hidden.
rules.startP: In the very first round, whoever holds the 7 of clubs (with 52 cards: the 2 of clubs) starts by playing it (alone or with other 7s/2s). From the second round on, the asshole of the last round always starts.
rules.t1p: Whoever starts a trick plays a single card or several cards of the same rank face up in the middle, for example two 8s or three jacks.
rules.t2p: The next player clockwise has to play the same number of cards, but of a higher rank. On two 8s you can play two 10s or two kings, but not a single ace.
rules.t3p: You may always pass instead, even if you could beat it. Passing doesn't lock you out: next time it's your turn in the same trick, you can join in again.
rules.ckQ: Two 9s are on the table. What may you play?
rules.trickP: A trick goes round the table as often as needed. Once everyone else has passed in a row, the last cards played win it: the whole pile is put aside face down and is out of the game. The player who won it leads the next trick with anything they like.
rules.trickNote: Nobody beats Dana's two kings. She wins the trick and leads the next one.
rules.outP: As soon as you have played your last card, you are out and get the highest rank still free. The others keep playing without you. If nobody beats your last cards, the next player still in the game (clockwise) leads the new trick.
rules.ranksH: Ranks and the end of a round
rules.ranksLead: The order in which players run out of cards decides their rank for the next round:
rules.ranksP: With 4 players there is no citizen, with 3 players there is no vice king and no vice asshole: just king, citizen and asshole. The king is often called president instead.
rules.endP: The round is over as soon as only one player still has cards. That player is the asshole and doesn't need to play out the rest.
rules.gameP: As many rounds as you like – the real fun starts in round two, when the ranks come into play. If you'd like a winner, keep score: 2 points for the king, 1 for the vice king. The first to 10 points wins.
rules.swLead: Before every new round, the losers have to pay up. The asshole gives their best cards to the king and only gets the king's worst cards in return. That's why it is so hard to climb back up.
rules.swAlt: The asshole gives the ace of spades and the king of hearts to the king. The king gives back the 7 of diamonds and the 8 of clubs.
rules.s1p: The asshole shuffles and deals all the cards, as at the start.
rules.s2p: The asshole gives their 2 highest cards to the king, the vice asshole gives their 1 highest card to the vice king. No choice here: it has to be the highest ones.
rules.s3p: The king gives the asshole 2 cards back, the vice king gives 1 to the vice asshole. These may be any cards – usually the lowest ones.
rules.s4p: Citizens don't swap. The asshole leads the first trick, and the round runs as before.
rules.swWhy: With only 3 players, only the king and the asshole swap, 1 card each. Tip for the asshole: you lead first, so start with your lowest cards while everybody can still beat them.
rules.varLead: Hardly any card game has as many house rules as Asshole. Agree on them before you start. A few common ones:
rules.var1: 10 high: the 10 ranks between king and ace, so the order is 7, 8, 9, J, Q, K, 10, A. Popular in parts of Germany with the Skat pack.
rules.var2: 2 is the highest card: in the English-speaking world, with 52 cards, the order often runs 3 up to ace and then 2 as the top card.
rules.var3: Equal cards allowed: you may also play the same rank, for example a 9 on a 9. Some groups then skip the next player.
rules.var4: Out after passing: whoever passes sits out until the trick is over.
rules.var5: Bomb: four cards of the same rank win any trick at once, no matter what lies there.
rules.var6: Revolution: whoever plays four of a kind turns the order around for the rest of the round: the 7 (or 2 with 52 cards) is now the highest card, the ace the lowest.
rules.var7: No ace at the end: whoever goes out with an ace automatically becomes the asshole.
rules.var8: The king picks: instead of getting the highest cards, the king names a rank (“Do you have an ace?”). If the asshole has one, they have to hand it over.
rules.var9: New seats: after every round everyone sits down in order of rank. The king stays put, the vice king sits to their left, and so on until the asshole on the king's right.
rules.var10: With jokers: jokers beat every other card, sometimes they may also stand in for any rank.
rules.var11: Keep your aces: aces are protected during the card swap – the asshole keeps them and hands over their next-highest cards instead.
rules.faq1q: Can I play more cards than the player before me?
rules.faq1a: No. You always play exactly as many cards as were led. With three jacks on a pair you can still play two of them and keep the third.
rules.faq2q: Do I have to play if I can?
rules.faq2a: No, passing is always allowed. It is often clever to save high cards and pass instead.
rules.faq3q: I passed – can I play again in the same trick?
rules.faq3a: Yes, in the standard rules you can. Only in the variant Out after passing do you have to wait for the next trick.
rules.faq4q: Does the asshole have to give away aces and kings?
rules.faq4a: Yes, always the highest cards, even if it hurts. Some groups agree that aces are kept – see Variants.
rules.faq5q: How is Asshole different from President?
rules.faq5a: It's the same family of games. Asshole is the usual German name, often with 32 cards and the ace as the top card. President mostly uses 52 cards, often with the 2 as the highest card, and many more house rules.
rules.faq6q: What else is the game called?
rules.faq6a: Besides President it is known as Scum, Bum, Rich Man Poor Man or Trou du cul in France. Commercial versions include The Great Dalmuti.
rules.faq7q: How many players do I need?
rules.faq7a: At least 3, best 4 to 6. With more than 5 players, use a 52-card pack so that everyone gets enough cards.
